universal_lens: The thermodynamic and mechanical perturbations of cold compression therapy induce a non-linear state transition in the muscle-tendon unit. This is mathematically unified as a time-dependent recovery operator acting on a multi-dimensional physiological phase space, mapping fatigue-induced deficits to homeostatic equilibrium across distinct biological subgroups.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the crossover trial outcomes into a hierarchical Bayesian framework. The between-subject factor (Population) acts as a prior hyperparameter, while within-subject factors (Condition, Time) drive posterior updates on recovery trajectories, allowing conformal prediction intervals for individualized athletic performance restoration.

primitives.name: Temporal Recovery Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Across populations, MVC was higher under CC than Sham from T2 to T4, with the largest between-condition difference at T4 (all p < .001).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: MVC: Maximum Voluntary Contraction (Newtons or Newton-meters); T_n: Discrete assessment timepoints (Hours); CC: Cold Compression condition; Sham: Control condition.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes monotonic recovery trajectory post-fatigue and that MVC serves as a linear proxy for neuromuscular functional capacity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur if prolonged cryotherapy blunts anabolic signaling, leading to a plateau or regression in MVC beyond T4.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a time-evolution operator in quantum mechanics, where the initial fatigued state vector evolves under the Hamiltonian of the CC protocol toward a ground state of maximal force production.
layer2.telemetry: Measured MVC force differentials between CC and Sham conditions at T2, T3, and T4.

primitives.name: Viscoelastic Damping Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Muscle stiffness was lower under CC from T2 to T4 (all p < .001).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Stiffness: Mechanical resistance to deformation (kPa or N/m); T_n: Discrete assessment timepoints (Hours).
primitives.assumptions: Treats the muscle tissue as a linear viscoelastic material where stiffness is inversely proportional to microvascular perfusion and fluid exchange.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if extreme temperatures cause localized vasoconstriction severe enough to impede metabolic waste clearance, paradoxically increasing stiffness.

layer2.mapping: Maps to a damping kernel in GSE's biomechanical engine, reducing the spring constant of the muscle-tendon unit to accelerate relaxation dynamics post-exertion.
layer2.telemetry: Shear wave elastography measurements of muscle stiffness pre- and post-intervention.

primitives.name: Demographic Phase Lag
primitives.verbatim_quote: Microvascular perfusion and pressure pain threshold were higher under CC at T2 - T4 overall (all p < .001), with earlier between-condition differences in MMA athletes and young adults and delayed differences in older adults.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Perfusion: Microvascular blood flow (Perfusion Units); PPT: Pressure Pain Threshold (kiloponds or kPa); Population: Categorical demographic variable.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes aging biology introduces a fixed temporal delay (phase lag) in the vascular and nociceptive response to external thermal/mechanical stimuli.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if pathological vascular occlusion exists, rendering the demographic phase lag infinite regardless of the applied CC protocol.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a frequency-dependent phase shift in control theory, where the 'older adult' system exhibits a lower bandwidth, requiring extended integration time to achieve the same output amplitude as younger systems.
layer2.telemetry: Laser Doppler flowmetry for perfusion and algometry for PPT across the three population cohorts.

Thus, the primitives collectively describe a bounded, non-linear dynamical system where optimal recovery is a function of precise timing and demographic-specific phase alignment.
